title: 18 kg of meth found on passenger from Singapore
detail: Customs said a 33-year-old NZ national arriving at Auckland Airport from Singapore had 18.45 kg of methamphetamine (street value about NZ$5.53 million) and was charged.

title: Glue drum explodes at Motueka wood-products site
detail: A glue drum exploded at a wood product manufacturing facility on Little Sydney Rd near Motueka; one worker was taken to Nelson Hospital in a serious condition. WorkSafe was notified and made initial inquiries.
agency: WorkSafe; Fire and Emergency NZ; St John
attribution: Per St John and WorkSafe as reported by 1News

title: Eleven vegetation fires in Canterbury; 22 ha burn near Napier
detail: Fire and Emergency NZ fought 11 vegetation fires across Canterbury, with 20 trucks and three helicopters at the Rotherham fire at peak; near Napier a Waitara Road fire burned 22 ha (18 ha plantation, 4 ha DOC bush). Heat and strong winds drove the blazes.
attribution: Per Fire and Emergency NZ as reported by 1News

title: Storm landslides kill 8 in Bay of Plenty; 9 dead in January system
detail: A subtropical low brought states of emergency to Whangārei, Thames-Coromandel, Hauraki, Bay of Plenty and Tairāwhiti; 1News reports six killed by a landslide at a Mount Maunganui holiday park, two in a Pāpāmoa house and one man swept away near Warkworth.
attribution: Civil Defence declarations and death toll via 1News

title: Record-setting rain: 274 mm in a day at Tauranga
detail: NIWA's January summary says tropical air on 18-22 January brought record-setting rainfall and flooding to much of the North Island and upper South Island; the month's highest 1-day total was 274 mm at Tauranga on 21 January, and Coromandel, Bay of Plenty and North Canterbury had 300-400%+ of normal January rain. (NIWA's page does not give a Whitianga figure.)
attribution: Climate data per NIWA monthly climate summary

title: NZ-supported Pacific op intercepts 4.2 t of cocaine
detail: Customs said Operation Kiwa, with NZDF and GCSB support, helped French authorities seize 4.24 tonnes (174 bales) of cocaine on the high seas off French Polynesia.

title: Woman arrested over alleged 18-year romance scam
detail: Police said a 44-year-old Auckland woman was charged with obtaining by deception after allegedly taking NZ$525,537 from a Dunedin victim in a romance scam dating back to 2006.

title: SH39 bridge near Puketotara collapses; ute drives into gap
detail: State Highway 39 Bridge 520, south of Mangati Road near Puketotara north of Ōtorohanga, partly collapsed in flooding after about 250-300 mm of rain in eight hours; a ute drove into the washout overnight and the occupant escaped unhurt.
attribution: As reported by NZ Herald; rainfall estimate per the report

title: Man dies in submerged vehicle on SH39; Ōtorohanga emergency
detail: A man was found dead in his vehicle after it was submerged by floodwaters on State Highway 39; Ōtorohanga Mayor Rodney Dow declared a district state of emergency and about 80 people were evacuated, many to Te Kotahitanga Marae. (The earlier summary's 'ute swept off SH39' is not how 1News or NZ Herald describe it: the fatality was a submerged vehicle near the Kiwi Road intersection, while a separate ute drove into a collapsed bridge and its occupant escaped.)
attribution: Per Ōtorohanga District Council and police as reported by 1News

title: Storm brings 240 km/h gust at Cape Turnagain; 30,000+ lose power
detail: Gusts reached 240 km/h at Cape Turnagain, up to 190 km/h on Wellington's high ground and about 130 km/h in the city; more than 30,000 properties lost power, about 23,000 on the Powerco network and about 10,000 in Wellington. Air New Zealand cancelled flights including Wellington services.
attribution: Wind and outage figures as reported by Anadolu, citing RNZ and Powerco

title: Storm disrupts flights, trains and ferries; Air NZ pauses three airports
detail: Reuters reported the storm disrupted flights, trains and ferries; Air New Zealand paused operations at Wellington, Napier and Palmerston North, with a few Wellington flights resuming by afternoon while cancellations stayed widespread. More than 30,000 properties were without power. (Reuters gives no operator-level train or Cook Strait ferry figures.)

title: Two travel-linked measles cases in Auckland household
detail: Health NZ confirmed two measles cases in one Auckland household linked to overseas travel; locations of interest included flight SQ281 from Singapore (arrived 17 February), Auckland Airport and Waitakere Hospital's emergency waiting room on 21 February.
attribution: Per Health NZ Medical Officer of Health as reported by 1News

title: Spark to block ~300 phones that cannot call 111 after 3G shutdown
detail: Spark said it would block about 300 mobile phones, mainly ASUS models, that cannot make emergency 111 calls once its 3G network shuts on 31 March 2026, calling them a significant safety risk; One NZ and 2degrees are also closing 3G.

title: Smuggled jewelled geckos repatriated from Netherlands
detail: DOC said six jewelled geckos seized by Dutch authorities in a 2023 Interpol-backed operation were repatriated; DOC said the species has never been legally exported, implying smuggling.

title: Emborg Emmentaler cheese recalled over Listeria
detail: New Zealand Food Safety recalled a batch of Emborg Emmentaler 200 g cheese (best before 4 November 2026) sold at supermarkets nationwide over possible Listeria; no illnesses were mentioned.
attribution: Recall notice by NZ Food Safety as reported by 1News

title: Meningococcal B cases among Dunedin students treated as outbreak
detail: Health NZ is treating two meningococcal B cases among Dunedin students (Otago Polytechnic hall on 7 March and University of Otago) as an outbreak; pharmacies reported high vaccine demand and some ran out of stock.
attribution: Per Health NZ as reported by 1News

title: Red heavy rain warning for eastern Northland
detail: MetService issued a Red warning (third of 2026) for Northland east of Kaikohe, Doubtless Bay to Whangārei, from 4pm 25 Mar to 4am 27 Mar, forecasting 270-320 mm with peak rates of 25-40 mm/h from a subtropical low.

title: About 500 evacuated in Kaitāia as rivers flood
detail: Around 500 people left homes near the Awanui and Pairatahi river confluence after roughly two months' rain fell in 24 hours; states of emergency were declared in Far North and Whangārei districts, with FENZ and USAR rescuing residents.

title: Boil-water notice for four Auckland suburbs lifted
detail: Watercare lifted a two-day boil-water notice for Hillsborough, Mt Roskill, Royal Oak and Three Kings after tracing E. coli detections to a single faulty water-quality sampling tap, which was replaced; thousands of residents had been affected.

title: Waikato state of emergency for Cyclone Vaianu
detail: Waikato CDEM declared a seven-day state of emergency at 9:32am on 11 Apr, ended 13 Apr; Port Waikato residents were displaced and SH25 was closed by slips between Coromandel Town–Whangapoua and Manaia–Thames.

title: Cyclone Vaianu crosses coast near Maketu, Bay of Plenty
detail: Reuters reported Vaianu made landfall on Sunday near the Maketu Peninsula in the Bay of Plenty, triggering floods, power outages and hundreds of evacuations; Whangārei had over 100 mm in 24 hours per MetService. (Corrects earlier 'landfall in Northland' dated 11 April.)

title: Air NZ cancels 90+ regional turboprop flights for Vaianu
detail: Air New Zealand cancelled more than 90 turboprop flights from regional North Island airports while jets and international services ran with delays; 270 mandatory evacuations were ordered in Whakatāne District and about 5,000 homes lost power.
attribution: Reuters report republished by Malay Mail

title: NZDF rejects China claims over P-8A flight
detail: NZDF said its P-8A Poseidon crew operated professionally and lawfully while monitoring North Korea sanctions evasion over the Yellow Sea and East China Sea, and that it had no data indicating disruption to civil aviation, after Chinese claims about the flight.

title: Wellington state of emergency after 77 mm in an hour
detail: Wellington Regional Emergency Management declared a state of emergency at 2:30pm on 20 Apr after the mayor cited 77 mm of rain in one hour at one site; Wainuiomata streets were evacuated, about 10 houses became uninhabitable and FENZ fielded 180+ calls in one morning.
attribution: WREMO, Wellington mayor and FENZ via The Spinoff

title: Wellington flood cancels flights and ferries
detail: 28 flights were cancelled at Wellington Airport, all Metlink harbour ferries were cancelled for two days, SH2 was cut to one lane near Melling and Riverside Drive in Lower Hutt closed.
attribution: Airport, Metlink and NZTA information via The Spinoff

title: Body of missing man found after Wellington floods
detail: Police found the body of a man missing since the floods in Karori; his car had been found in Karori Stream. Newtown and Island Bay businesses were damaged and shelters were opened.

title: RNZAF P-8A spots possible DPRK sanctions breach
detail: NZDF said an RNZAF P-8A patrol over the Yellow Sea and East China Sea recorded a possible ship-to-ship transfer in breach of UN sanctions on North Korea, logged 35 vessels of interest and broadcast 8 deterrence messages.

title: 39 kg of meth seized at Wellington Airport
detail: Customs said two women aged 21 and 22 arriving from Malaysia via Sydney had 39 kg of methamphetamine (up to NZ$13 million) disguised as tea in suitcases; both were charged with importing a Class A drug.

title: NZDF and Customs fly Pacific surveillance under Operation Kiwa
detail: NZDF said an MC-12K and a P-8A patrolled the EEZs of Fiji, Niue and the Cook Islands in May under the Customs-led Operation Kiwa against transnational crime, photographing vessels possibly engaged in illegal activity for follow-up.
agency: New Zealand Defence Force / NZ Customs

title: 100 kg of cocaine found in Tauranga reefer container
detail: Customs said x-ray found 100 kg of cocaine (up to NZ$35 million) hidden by rip-on/rip-off in a container loaded in Chile via Peru, Colombia and Panama at the Port of Tauranga.

title: Anti-Scam Alliance widens bank, telco and platform measures
detail: Minister Cameron Brewer announced wider Confirmation of Payee, an Online Scams Code backed by Google, Meta and TikTok, and a telco blocking code; a six-month pilot blocked 23,000+ domains and prevented about NZ$23.8 million in losses. MBIE cites NZ$265 million in bank-reported fraud losses in the year to Oct 2025.
attribution: Minister and Anti-Scam Alliance via SecurityBrief

title: NCSC Q1: NZ$5.6m lost, first 'highly significant' incidents since 2021/22
detail: NCSC handled 1,164 reports in Jan-Mar 2026 with NZ$5.6 million direct loss (NZ$5.2 million from individuals); three C2 incidents were the first of that class since 2021/22.

title: DIA issues formal AML warnings to 10 reporting entities
detail: DIA, sole AML/CFT supervisor from 1 July 2026, issued formal warnings to six Auckland law firms and a payment provider, real estate agent, accountant and lender for failing to get required independent audits.

title: About 200 Wellington flights cancelled in southerly storm
detail: Around 200 flights were cancelled at Wellington Airport as winds near 100 km/h hit, with gusts over 150 km/h at Mt Kaukau; SH2 near Kaitoke was blocked by a fallen tree and more than 4,000 properties lost power on the Wellington Electricity network.
attribution: Per Wellington Airport and Wellington Electricity as reported by 1News

title: 7,000+ lower North Island customers lose power in storm
detail: More than 7,000 customers in the lower North Island lost power: 5,280 on the Powerco network (3,000+ in Taranaki, 1,300+ in Whanganui) and 1,789 in Wellington; about 200 flights were grounded and ferry sailings cancelled.
attribution: Outage figures per lines companies as reported by Insurance Business

title: 24 arrested, NZ$1.95m assets seized in Waikato gang probe
detail: Police said an investigation into Comanchero, Mongols and Mongrel Mob members in Waikato and Auckland led to 24 arrests and seizure of NZ$1.95 million in assets, 2.5 kg meth, 134 kg pseudoephedrine intercepted by Customs and firearms.

title: Red rain warning for coastal Dunedin and Clutha
detail: MetService issued a Red Heavy Rain Warning from noon 5 Jul to 9am 6 Jul for coastal Dunedin and Clutha, forecasting 80-120 mm; Otago Regional Council flagged Taieri Plains, Milton and the Clutha Delta for flooding and Dunedin's EOC was activated.
attribution: MetService warning via Otago Regional Council

title: First H5N1 bird flu confirmed in NZ, in skua at Petone
detail: H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b was confirmed in a brown skua found on Petone Beach, Wellington, New Zealand's first detection; MPI widened wildlife surveillance. Biosecurity Minister Andrew Hoggard said the public health risk is low.
attribution: Per MPI and the Biosecurity Minister as reported by 1News

title: M5.9 quake north of Te Anau prompts brief tsunami alert
detail: A magnitude 5.9 earthquake (first assessed as 6.3) struck about 40 km north of Te Anau at 9:14 pm NZST; NEMA issued then cancelled a tsunami alert after no signals were detected. More than 18,000 felt reports went to GeoNet, with no immediate damage or injuries reported.
attribution: Per GeoNet and NEMA as reported by SBS

title: Fake-police callers draining crypto holders
detail: Police warned of a rise in calls from fake detectives who steer victims to fake crypto sites to harvest seed phrases; Police said some victims lost millions.

title: M5.9 Taumarunui quake, largest recorded there; highways shut by slips
detail: A shallow magnitude 5.9 quake (9 km deep) struck 5 km south-west of Taumarunui at 4:51 am, felt by over 22,000 people; windows broke and stock fell but no injuries were reported. 79 aftershocks followed within hours, and SH3 through the Awakino Gorge and SH43 were closed.
agency: GeoNet (Earth Sciences New Zealand); NZ Transport Agency
attribution: Per GeoNet seismologists as reported by 1News

title: Christchurch man faces trafficking, migrant exploitation charges
detail: Immigration NZ laid 35 charges under the Crimes and Immigration Acts, including trafficking in persons, against a Christchurch man over alleged exploitation of 11 victims.

title: Auckland flu admissions highest since 2015
detail: Health NZ said 177 people were admitted with flu to four Auckland hospitals in 9-16 August, up from 125 the week before and the highest weekly rate since 2015, driven by influenza A(H3N2) subclade K alongside RSV and rhinovirus.
attribution: Admission figures per Health NZ as reported by 1News

title: NCSC Q2: scams lead incident reports; losses fall to NZ$2.7m
detail: NCSC handled 1,129 reports in Apr-Jun 2026; scams and fraud were the top category (348 reports, about NZ$860,000 lost) and total direct loss fell 52% to NZ$2.7 million. It flagged QR-code phishing at Christchurch parking meters.

title: Transpower grid fault cuts power to 25,000 in Southland
detail: A national grid fault on the Transpower network around midday cut power to about 25,000 PowerNet customers in Southland and parts of Otago for about two hours, during an orange wind warning with lightning damage; about 300 remained off that evening.
attribution: Per Transpower and PowerNet as reported by 1News

title: Scrub fire at Albert Town, Wānaka, forces 22 households out
detail: A fire through about 1 km of trees and scrub behind houses at Albert Town was fought by eight crews in windy conditions; 22 households were evacuated as a precaution and no houses burned. It was contained by 11 pm; the cause was unknown.
agency: Fire and Emergency New Zealand; Police

title: Trans-Tasman crackdown: 85 NZ raids, 34 charged
detail: Police said a 14-18 Sep joint NZ-Australia operation produced 85 raids and 34 people charged in NZ, seizing 6,183 cannabis plants, 30 kg meth, opium, 4 firearms and NZ$647,690 cash; Auckland grow houses were linked to Vietnamese organised crime.

title: NZ warships transit Taiwan Strait, reportedly tracked by PLA
detail: NZDF confirmed HMNZS Te Mana and HMNZS Aotearoa transited the Taiwan Strait during a three-month deployment; Chinese forces reportedly tracked the ships.
attribution: NZDF confirmation via Stuff; tracking claim is reported

title: Head Hunters case: laundering via crypto accounts alleged
detail: Court documents in Police's Operation Juneau allege North Shore Head Hunters proceeds were laundered through financial and crypto accounts, funding luxury travel and a Dubai car-hire business; a founding member charged with money laundering has pleaded not guilty, trial March 2027.
agency: NZ Police National Organised Crime Group
